I re-read every repository file the output cites (file:ap_aging/src/ap_aging/aging.py, file:ap_aging/ci.py, file:ap_aging/CLAUDE.md) and re-ran the repository-wide search for secret use, so each citation now resolves to a read in this attempt. The method is the same as attempt 1. I used feat.tasks to find the Backend tasks (TSK-05, TSK-06 in ap_aging) and checked whether they need external access: both are pure functions with no transport. I confirmed from the code and CI that no credentials or environment variables are read, and compared the result with the permission table's grant through tool:repo-access (none). Then I rewrote task.secrets_scope in full, with names only and the attempt number updated. The file on disk had an extra line appended after my content ('[Tool result] [ap_aging] Tool registry: ...'). It is not part of the output template, so I left it out of the full rewrite. Its content is already covered by the tool:repo-access citation in section 3. I did not use the osv or pypi connectors because they have nothing to do with secrets.

claims.text: The Backend tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-05 (STORY-05) and TSK-06 (STORY-06), both in the ap_aging repository.
TSK-05 adds a pure function overdue_with_risk(invoices, as_of, risk_by_vendor). TSK-06 adds overdue_rows_to_json(rows) with no transport layer, because a transport would re-trigger DES-01.
The tasks use only the Python 3.9 standard library and add no new technology.
The current ap_aging source module imports only datetime, decimal and typing, and makes no network, file or environment access.

The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. It compiles, runs the unit tests under coverage, applies the coverage gate and runs static checks locally, without reading credentials or environment variables.
No secrets are required or granted for ap_aging under the permission table, so required and granted access match and no access request is needed.
The only external-provider touchpoint in the feature is TSK-04 in the Data Science lane (acme-llm, pending TQ-8), which is outside Backend scope.
